reading: This operator record, labeled SONM in the source facility data, is almost certainly a mislabeling of State Of New Mexico rather than a reference to the blockchain company SONM, short for Supercomputing Organized by Network Mining, a decentralized fog computing marketplace built on the Ethereum blockchain. The registry's associated facility, the John F. Simms Building in Santa Fe, is confirmed through New Mexico's own Department of Information Technology and General Services Department materials to be a state government office complex, part of the State Capitol's South Complex, and a documented mid-century modern architectural landmark that has housed New Mexico state offices including IT operations. This registry found no evidence connecting the blockchain company SONM to any facility in Santa Fe, New Mexico, making the state government explanation far more plausible than a literal reading of the operator name as the crypto project. This case is analogous to other name-collision and mistagging issues already flagged in this registry, such as Duke Libraries and Dennis Sampier, where a facility record's operator field did not describe what it appeared to at first glance, and underscores this registry's standing policy against matching entities on name alone. Pending further confirmation, this record is treated as New Mexico state government IT infrastructure housed in the Simms Building rather than as the blockchain company.
